messages:
anna: Hey — ran an nsys capture for the 2.1.3 batcher run. Timeline looks like memcpy H2D on stream 3 blocking kernels on stream 0, but kernel execution shows gaps. https://perf.link/xyz (private)

mike: can you paste the CLI you used?

anna: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=batcher_2_1_3 nsys-output.qdrep` then `nsys stats batcher_2_1_3.qdrep` and exported the timeline to .sqlite for traceview.

sasha: quick q — were you using pinned hostpool or default allocator?

anna: pinned hostpool enabled for this run. config: `hostpool: pinned`, `kv_prefetch_threads: 4`, `batch_size: dynamic`.

jamal: interesting. I see TX memcpy on copy engine (stream 3) starting right before kernel on stream 0 but kernel shows a ~6ms lull. On CPU side there's a 6ms user thread preemption right then.

anna: exactly. my theory: host thread is yielding mid-prefetch, so prefetch doesn't actually populate the GPU pages in time; kernel waits on page faults or on copy completion which looks serialized in the timeline.

sasha: can you paste the relevant waterfall snippet? even a small ascii excerpt helps.

anna: sure — exported snippet from traceview timeline (trimmed):
```
[0.000s] memcpy HtoD (stream 3) size=48MB -> cudaMemcpyAsync
[0.001s] kernel conv_forward (stream 0) grid=...
[0.007s] cpu sched-out (worker-thread 42)
[0.013s] memcpy HtoD complete (stream 3)
[0.014s] kernel resumes # actually starts executing heavy ops
```

mike: that matches the CPU sched gap aligning with the hostcopy window. So the apparent memcpy->kernel overlap is illusory: kernel launch is enqueued but the GPU doesn't get all pages until hostcopy completes, which itself got delayed by CPU preempt.

jamal: Another possibility: unified memory page faulting if prefetch didn't actually fault in pages ahead. But you used explicit pinned memcpy, right?

anna: yes, explicit async memcpy pinned->device. No UM in this path.

sasha: two actionable checks:
- reproduce with `isolcpus` or SCHED_FIFO for worker threads to eliminate CPU preempt.
- run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` briefly to confirm dependency timing (will serialize everything but shows order).

anna: ran a quick SCHED_FIFO run on a dev node — the 6ms lull disappears and memcpy finishes before kernel heavy phase. Throughput improved ~12% on that trace.

mike: nice. Do we think this is flaky on noisy hosts or specific to our batcher heuristic (kv prefetch thread count)?

anna: likely both. With kv_prefetch_threads=2 the hostcopies are more bursty (longer single-threaded memcpy windows) and more vulnerable to preempt. With 4 threads copies overlap better and are shorter, but more contention on PCIe throughput and CPU.

jamal: TL;DR: host scheduling jitter can make async H2D appear to serialize kernels. Fixes: increase prefetch threads, pin prefetch threads to cores, or use background pinned DMA engine pool to amortize.

sasha: also consider switching to a dedicated copy stream with `cudaMemcpyAsync` from a thread that never blocks on app work (separate host thread pool pinned to isolated cores).

mike: can we add a lightweight perf test in CI that simulates CPU preemption? e.g. spawn a low-priority kernel that steals CPU for X ms while copying.

ci-bot: created ticket INF-4021: add host-sched-noise test + SLO for memcpy-kernel overlap. Assigned to @jamal.

jamal: I'll take INF-4021. Plan: 1) microbench on dev nodes, 2) instrument runtime to record host-thread sched-in/out around prefetch, 3) add opt flag `prefetch_worker_affinity: true`.

anna: also noticed a pattern where nvtx ranges for kvcache prefetch show repeated small memcpys that fall back to hostcopy when pinned pool exhausted. We should log pool saturation in dev traces.

sasha: good call — add a meter on pinned pool usage. If pool saturation correlates with serialization, we can autotune pool size.

mike: final note — when writing the postmortem for the perf regression we should include both the nsys waterfall and a CPU sched trace (perf or osrt) stacked. That makes it obvious it's host-side.

anna: agreed. I'll attach the nsys export + perf trace to INF-4021. Cheers :thumbsup!
